title: MT82 Gearshift Controls — Overview
introduction:
This overview covers the external controls for the MT82 six-speed manual transmission. The gear knob gets the attention, but the lever assembly carries your movement toward the gearbox.

I separate that movement path from the parts inventory below. The nested items belong with the gearshift lever assembly; the knob and gearshift lever boot are listed separately. This is a guide to the arrangement and its operation, rather than instructions for removal, adjustment or rebuilding.

edits.text: The manual transmission’s external controls comprise the following assemblies and parts:
edits.why: The list identifies the controls outside the gearbox. Its nesting keeps the lever assembly’s associated service items together.

edits.text: Gearshift lever assembly, with the associated items below
Service kit containing a roll pin, spring, plastic blocker, shoulder bolt and anti-rattle washer
edits.why: These are the stated kit contents; the inventory does not establish their installation order.

edits.text: Tunnel seal, foam gasket and boot

edits.why: Retained as a separate inventory entry from the boot listed with the lever assembly’s tunnel seal and foam gasket.

edits.text: How Lever Movement Reaches the Transmission
The driver controls the manual transmission with the floor-mounted gearshift lever in the floor console. Moving that lever transmits movement through a lever attached to the transmission.
edits.why: This describes the mechanical selection path. Clutch release is a separate function, so the parts inventory alone cannot explain or diagnose every difficult shift.
